title: LRP37 Method Protocol
author: Gaku Takahashi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bck8iuzw
materials: Blood is collected with a heparinized syringe.
Use the supernatant as leukocyte-rich plasma (LRP).

steps.title: Equilibrate reagents and blood
steps.instruction: Prepare the temperature of the dextran solution and blood sample.

substeps.instruction: Incubate 0.6% dextran solution at 37 °C for approximately 5 minutes.
Equilibrate blood at 37 °C for a few minutes.

steps.title: Separate plasma using dextran
steps.instruction: Mix blood with dextran to form a supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 μl of blood to 800 μl of dextran.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 10 to 30 minutes until a supernatant is formed.

steps.title: Dilute LRP with pretreatment solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10-fold dilution of the LRP.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 μl of LRP to 900 μl of pretreatment solution (0.02% tween, FUJI FILM Wako Pure Chemical Incorporation, Osaka, Japan).

steps.title: Lyse white blood cells
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt white blood cells in the diluted LRP.

substeps.instruction: Mix the 10-times diluted LRP five times with a vortex mixer at 3000 rpm for 10 s.

steps.title: Inactivate interfering factors
steps.instruction: Heat and cool the mixture to remove factors that interfere with the limulus test.

substeps.instruction: Heat the mixture at 70 °C for 10 minutes.
Cool the mixture at 0 °C for 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Perform endotoxin-specific limulus test
steps.instruction: React the processed sample with endotoxin-specific reagent.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 μL of the mixture to a freeze-dried endotoxin-specific limulus test (Endotoxin Single test Wako, FUJI FILM Wako) to dissolve the reagent.
Place the test tube in the TOXINOMETER (FUJI FILUM Wako) and react at 37 °C for up to 200 minutes.

steps.title: Calculate endotoxin content
steps.instruction: Determine the endotoxin concentration based on gelation time and dilution factors.

substeps.instruction: Define the start transmitted light as 100% and the gelation time (min) as the time when turbidity is reduced to 92%.
Create a calibration curve using at least three different doses of standard endotoxin (E. coli O111:B4).
Multiply the calculated endotoxin amount by 10 to account for the pretreatment solution dilution.
Calculate final endotoxin content in LRP using the formula: (A + dextran volume)/A, where A = blood volume - (blood volume × haematocrit value/100).
